summary: The ADR sets clear principles but is far from implementable as written: its biggest gap is scope, since it never says whether the deliverable is an automated runner that launches and drives agents or a manual method with templates and an optional observer.

questions.text: Is the deliverable an automated harness that launches and drives the fresh agent, or a manual protocol with tooling only for setup, capture and reporting?
questions.reason: Decides the largest scope and ownership split (per-harness launchers vs checklists); the ADR only says to start a fresh agent and points to external method docs.

questions.text: Are observable outcome checks executable predicates over the resulting KB/artifacts, a reviewer rubric, or both?
questions.reason: Executable checks need a check language, runner and pass/fail records; the ADR only says to independently inspect results against task outcomes.

questions.text: Does the observer attach as an external proxy or as a config-gated hook inside the MCP adapter, and which component owns it?
questions.reason: Determines code ownership and whether internal state is visible; the ADR places it at the adapter boundary and rules out a per-function effect or production ledger.

questions.text: Is sanitization of committed reports automated with defined redaction rules or a manual review gate, and what counts as payload?
questions.reason: It is the guarantee that private payloads never get committed; the ADR only says sanitized reports may be committed.

questions.text: What is the on-disk format and manifest schema of a scenario package?
questions.reason: Fixes the loader and validator; the ADR lists the package parts but defers shape to the external README.

questions.text: What identifies a scenario revision: a manifest version field, a content hash, or the git commit?
questions.reason: Run records must pin it and comparability depends on it; the ADR says packages are versioned and revisions recorded, not how.

questions.text: What is the trace event schema: what operation ID refers to, the unit of response volume, where selected snapshot/candidate comes from, and the sink format?
questions.reason: Fixes the persisted event struct and whether the product must expose IDs; the ADR names the fields but not their definitions or encoding.

questions.text: How are corrections appended to a run record: entries in the report, separate linked files, or git history, and is immutability enforced?
questions.reason: Decides run IDs, amendment schema and enforcement; the ADR sets the append-not-rewrite rule but no mechanism.

questions.text: Is the field report a structured machine-checked record with typed finding links, or a free-form markdown template?
questions.reason: Structured findings need a schema and link validation; the ADR names the report halves and the four links each finding needs, deferring templates to the README.

questions.text: How are CLI/file-edit fallback and human intervention captured: transcript parsing, harness hooks, operator logging or self-report?
questions.reason: Each source needs different code and yields different observation gaps; the ADR says record them when available and state gaps.

questions.text: What are the transcript retention policy's terms (location, duration, deletion) and does tooling enforce them?
questions.reason: Decides storage paths, gitignore and cleanup tooling; the ADR requires transcripts stay local under an explicit policy it does not state.

questions.text: Does the harness need first-class repeated-run batching and cross-run comparison, or is comparison left to reviewers?
questions.reason: Batch support needs grouping and aggregate views; the ADR requires repeating important comparisons and forbids call-count scores but says nothing on tooling.

questions.text: What does cache condition mean concretely, and must the harness control it or only record it?
questions.reason: Decides which caches are reset or probed per run; the ADR lists cache condition among recorded fields without defining it.

questions.text: Is the agent's account a single reflection response or a structured protocol, sent in the same session, with a recorded phase where the evaluator's interpretation is shown back?
questions.reason: Shapes the agent-experience record and session continuity needs; the ADR orders account before interpretation and names a short reflection prompt.

questions.text: How is the restricted MCP-only condition enforced: harness tool allowlist, sandbox, or prompt instruction?
questions.reason: Changes what is built per harness and what tool catalog is recorded; the ADR requires the condition be labelled but not how it is enforced.

questions.text: Is the seeded KB a committed fixture snapshot or produced by a deterministic seeding script, rebuilt fresh for every run?
questions.reason: Decides seeding code vs snapshot refresh process; the ADR says only synthetic seeded and disposable KBs.

questions.text: What happens to the disposable KB and destinations after a run: kept for inspection, archived into the record, or torn down, and who cleans up?
questions.reason: Independent inspection needs the end state to survive; the ADR says disposable KBs but nothing on lifecycle or cleanup ownership.

questions.text: What baseline environment do installation/readiness scenarios start from, and does the harness provision it?
questions.reason: Moves the harness boundary (VM image vs fresh user); the ADR only says not to assume a developer's prepared machine.

questions.text: How are web/human-surface interactions observed when instrumentation is defined only at the MCP adapter boundary?
questions.reason: May need a second observer and cross-surface correlation; the ADR puts web handoffs in scenarios and defers cross-surface evaluation to ADR 0023.

questions.text: What are the run-record status values and flags (partial/failed/cancelled/assisted, simulated human), and is assisted a status or a separate flag?
questions.reason: Persisted closed value sets drive filtering; the ADR names the outcomes that must stay visible and requires simulated-human labels, not their encoding.

questions.text: What ends a run: agent-declared done, a time/turn/token budget, or operator cancellation?
questions.reason: Decides termination logic and how partial/failed/cancelled statuses are assigned; the ADR names the statuses but no budgets or criteria.
